title: How David Goggins builds mental toughness: the cookie jar and a new norm
summary: Goggins describes doubting himself in his first Hell Week, then using the "cookie jar" of past hardships to flip his mindset from "I don't belong" to "I'm the most trained person here." He argues SEAL candidates quit because their minds are untrained, and that you must know your why to answer the negative questions that surface under pain.

principles.text: Use the cookie jar: recall past hardships you overcame when you want to quit.
principles.quote: you have to remind yourself we all have a story we've all all of us have gone through very hard times but we're in a hard time our mind has a way of forgetting Woodall we've overcome

principles.text: Reframe your painful past as the ultimate training ground, not as something unfair.
principles.quote: I look at my life and how I came up as the ultimate training ground versus most people look at it as why what was me God why exactly why

principles.text: The mind takes the path of least resistance when friction hits, but friction is what causes growth.
principles.quote: your mind has a good way of taking the path of least resistance whenever friction happens friction causes growth

principles.text: Repeat a new daily self-narrative until you believe it; hardship becomes your new norm.
principles.quote: so that's what became my daily voice was you really are the baddest person all right planet yeah after a period of time you start to believe that

principles.text: Physical training alone builds quitters; the mind is the most powerful weapon and must be trained.
principles.quote: we were building bigger stronger faster quitters why is that if you don't work on the one thing the most powerful weapon in the world is your mind

principles.text: Know your why so you can answer the negative questions that come up in pain, or you will quit.
principles.quote: you have to know why am I here for me when I was going through still training I was willing to die so all these negative questions that kept on coming up in my head I had I the answer
